audience: Indie game developers and small studios who need game-ready GLB assets but cannot hand-model every prop, weapon, and character.
problem: A game project needs hundreds of modeled, budgeted GLB assets and hand-modeling them is slow; raw AI text-to-3D output does not help because it arrives unverified — broken meshes, blown triangle budgets, missing materials — and ships straight into the game.
promise: Your AI sculpts your game assets.

hero.headline: Your AI sculpts your game assets.
hero.lede: Glina turns a text prompt into a verified, game-ready GLB. A Brama-routed model writes Blender Python and runs it in a live Blender MCP session. A structural gate passes or fails the result before it counts as done.

approvedClaims.claim: Glina turns a text prompt into a verified, game-ready GLB: a Brama-routed model writes Blender Python and executes it through a live Blender MCP session.
Every result passes a structural quality gate before it counts as done; the gate fails the job and never warns.
The gate checks a valid glTF container, mesh/primitive sanity, a triangle budget (default 6000 ±100%), materials/skins/animation presence, file-size bounds, and an optional Blender render smoke.
Secrets are handled only through Skarbiec: config holds `skarbiec://<item>/<field>` refs and the loader rejects inline secrets and credential-shaped environment variables.
Browser automation runs only through the Weles MCP stdio server (`weles-mcp`), never a local Chromium profile.
Blender is driven only through a Blender MCP server (`uvx blender-mcp` by default), never hand-rolled sockets.
Model access goes only through Brama, the Wisent model router; there is no direct provider API code in the package — direct paths were deleted at the owner's demand, not gated.
Installation is `npm install -g @wisent-ai/glina`, and the package ships two bins: `glina` (CLI) and `glina-mcp` (MCP stdio server for agents).

The `glina` CLI covers check-config, sculpt, create, verify, blender-health, and weles-tools, and the `glina-mcp` stdio server exposes the same surface to agent hosts as six tools: glina_create_asset, glina_sculpt, glina_verify_asset, glina_check_config, glina_blender_health, and glina_weles_tools.
`kamien.glb`, a granite boulder with moss patches, was generated end-to-end over 12 bpy rounds through Brama and the Blender MCP session and passed the verification gate on 2026-07-27.
`krasnolud-wojownik.glb`, a dwarven warrior, was generated through local Brama and passed the verification gate on 2026-07-28.

Born as the asset pipeline of the browser RTS simple-rts-unity (`web/art/`, extracted with full history), Glina now ships as a standalone Wisent product with a CLI package and a macOS desktop app (`wisent-ai/glina-desktop`).

requiredProof: A real terminal transcript of `npm install -g @wisent-ai/glina` followed by `glina check-config` validating the config and its Skarbiec vault references.
A real terminal transcript of `glina verify assets/models/kamien.glb` passing the structural GLB quality gate.
A factual table of the proven live results: kamien.glb (granite boulder with moss patches, 2026-07-27) and krasnolud-wojownik.glb (dwarven warrior, 2026-07-28), both gate-verified.
Real output of `glina blender-health` probing the Blender session and `glina weles-tools` listing the browser-layer tools.

rules: Type comes from the three families in wisent-components/tokens.json: `font.expanded` ('Hubot Sans Expanded') for display headings, `font.sans` ('Hubot Sans') for body and UI, `font.mono` ('IBM Plex Mono') for every command, transcript, and code artifact. No fourth family.
One dominant foreground/background relationship: `color.background` #f8fdfb behind `color.ink` #2d3130 body copy, with `color.canvasMuted` #ecf2f0 as the only alternating section band.
Headings and deep surfaces use `color.forest` / `color.brand900` #273329; supporting copy uses `color.secondaryText` #59605d and `color.mutedText` #8b9290.

The accent role is restrained and reserved for the single primary action: `color.brand` / `color.brand500` #9ecca0 with `color.brandHover` #8dbb8f, and `color.brandLink` #769978 for inline links. Tints are for quiet surfaces only, never large filled blocks.
Rules, card edges, and table borders use `color.border` #dee4e2 and `color.borderStrong` #c1c8c6; `color.subtleBorder` #eeeeee for the lightest dividers.
`color.success`, `color.warning`, and `color.danger` are reserved for real product status — a passed versus failed verification gate — never for decoration.
Spacing and section rhythm use the `space` scale (2px through 40px); corners use the `radius` scale (6px through 22px); depth uses `shadow.surface` and `shadow.raised` only.
Motion stays inside `motion.fast` 150ms and `motion.standard` 180ms, must explain state, sequence, or causality, and must respect reduced-motion preferences.
Terminal evidence is real captured output rendered in `font.mono`, never a drawn window; the two preview PNGs are real captured renders of the proven assets.
forbidden: Interchangeable AI gradients, floating glass cards, excessive rounded rectangles, and decorative grids.
Fake terminal chrome or any drawn, dressed-up, or retyped terminal that is not real captured Glina output.
Motion that does not explain state, sequence, or causality.
Inventing a new logo, font, palette, or claim because a canonical asset is inconvenient to locate.
Copying another company's copy, layout, illustration, product UI, or brand assets.
Invented social proof or performance numbers: no customer names, no adoption counts, no asset-count or time-saved figures beyond the two proven runs.
Claims of direct provider API access; every model call goes through Brama.
Generic slogans that omit the product or the outcome.
Placeholder product screenshots presented as real.
Publishing before the CTA destination and analytics ownership are known.
Treating a visual-model score as proof of functional correctness.

kamien.glb (2026-07-27) and krasnolud-wojownik.glb (2026-07-28) are the only generations the page may present as evidence; no other runs are claimed.
